candidate_under_test: Execute effect first, then let both writers CAS/create the same successor receipt; CAS loser reads winner and avoids replay on later reconstruction.
adversarial_trace: A and B both reconstruct predecessor P and derive the same logical effect id E and successor path S(E).
A executes logical effect E before S(E) exists.
B also executes logical effect E before S(E) exists.
B loses the create/CAS race, reads A's valid S(E), and stops.
Final repository state has one canonical successor but the logical effect executed twice.
falsification: Final-successor CAS performed after effect execution is too late to guarantee zero duplicate logical effects. A unique canonical receipt does not imply unique execution.

revision.name: deterministic pre-effect claim barrier
revision.claim_path: role-local immutable exact path derived solely from effect_id
protocol: Each writer reconstructs P and derives the same effect_id and claim_path.
Before executing the logical effect, each writer attempts create-if-absent of claim_path.
Exactly one successful creator becomes the only writer authorized to execute the effect.
A create/CAS loser reads the existing claim, validates predecessor_blob/effect_id/task binding, and returns without executing or replaying the effect.
The winner executes once, writes the artifact and successor terminal receipt bound to the claim, then advances LATEST by guarded update.
revision.reason: All executions are dominated by a single create-if-absent claim event; the losing writer is excluded before the effect boundary rather than after it.

ordering_checks.A_claims_first: one authorized executor A; B performs zero effect executions
ordering_checks.B_claims_first: one authorized executor B; A performs zero effect executions
ordering_checks.post_effect_final_CAS_candidate: two executions possible before one canonical successor is selected

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: bounded exact-path claim/state/evidence transport only; no hosted compute
mechanism_assessment.open_reason: Crash-after-claim and transient exact-path visibility have not yet been shown to recover without duplicate execution or false completion.

exact_next_action: On the next valid invocation, test one winner-crash-after-claim interleaving for the deterministic pre-effect claim barrier. Require no second executor to run without a role-local recovery certificate, no ambiguous missing-path read to count as completion, and preserve the still-untested transient exact-path-not-visible case as the following continuation. Persist/read back one bounded result and stop.
